tools.name: search_addresses
tools.description: Lists the addresses at a UK postcode, each with its UPRN and display address. Broadband availability differs per property, so the other tools take a UPRN and display address to answer for one exact property.

tools.name: find_broadband_deals
tools.description: Returns the broadband deals available at a UK address or postcode: a best value, cheapest and fastest pick plus a provider-varied list. Each deal has its monthly price, contract length, speed and true whole-contract cost, with intro pricing, later price rises and setup fees included. Optional filters: budget, minimum speed, provider, contract length, no mid-contract rises, mobile and satellite broadband. The precision field says whether results are for one property or the whole postcode.

uprn.description: Property identifier (UPRN) from search_addresses. With it, results are for that exact property instead of the whole postcode. An internal reference, not meaningful to the user.

address_label.description: The display_address the user picked from search_addresses, passed back verbatim. Carried into the switch link so the FindBroadband site greets the user with their address instead of asking again.

max_monthly_price.description: Budget cap in GBP per month, from phrases like 'under £30'.

min_speed_mbps.description: Minimum download speed in Mbps. Typical needs: email and browsing about 35, two people working from home plus gaming about 150, a heavy 4K household about 300.

provider.description: Only show deals from this provider, when the user names one.

max_contract_months.description: Longest contract the user will accept, e.g. 12 for 'no long contracts'.

exclude_mid_contract_rises.description: true when the user says they want no mid-contract price rises.

include_mobile_broadband.description: Include 4G/5G home broadband and fixed wireless. Default false: deals on a line only.

include_satellite.description: Include satellite broadband (Starlink). Default false. Satellite needs a dish and has an upfront cost.

tools.name: check_if_overpaying
tools.description: Compares what a user pays for broadband, or a renewal price their provider quoted, against comparable deals available at their address. Returns a computed verdict, the saving over 24 months and the best alternatives, each with its true cost over 24 months.

uprn.description: Property identifier (UPRN) from search_addresses. With it, results are for that exact property instead of the whole postcode. An internal reference, not meaningful to the user.

address_label.description: The display_address the user picked from search_addresses, passed back verbatim. Carried into the switch link so the FindBroadband site greets the user with their address instead of asking again.

monthly_bill.description: What the user currently pays per month in GBP (or the renewal price quoted to them).

current_speed_mbps.description: The user's current download speed in Mbps. Package names often carry it: 'M125' is about 132.

current_provider.description: The user's current broadband provider, as they said it, e.g. 'Sky' or 'Virgin Media'.

quote_type.description: 'renewal_offer' when the user is evaluating a renewal or retention price their provider quoted; 'current_bill' (default) when it is what they pay today.

tools.name: get_deal_details
tools.description: Returns the full terms of one deal from an earlier result: setup costs, price-rise terms, what happens after the intro period, the whole-contract total and whether the deal is available at the user's address.

deal_id.description: The deal_id from a previous find_broadband_deals or check_if_overpaying result.

postcode.description: The user's postcode. With it, availability is checked at their address.

uprn.description: Property identifier (UPRN) from search_addresses. With it, results are for that exact property instead of the whole postcode. An internal reference, not meaningful to the user.

address_label.description: The display_address the user picked from search_addresses, passed back verbatim. Carried into the switch link so the FindBroadband site greets the user with their address instead of asking again.
